tldr: A TuxCare sales pitch for its patched open-source package repository, end-of-life security support and rebootless Linux kernel patching, framed by statistics on unpatched systems and supply-chain malware.
summary: Sven Sellen, TuxCare's director of global enterprise sales, opens with survey figures on patching. He said 93% of organisations knew they were vulnerable before an incident, yet 49% saw no improvement in patching speed and 43% cannot take systems offline to patch. He cited more than 455,000 new malicious packages last year, 1.23 million in total across npm, PyPI and Maven, with 99% of 2025's open-source malware on npm. He also pointed to EU CRA, PCI DSS and FedRAMP compliance pressure.

The rest is a product tour. SecureChain is a curated repository that malware-scans and rebuilds packages from source, ships SBOMs, VEX and SLSA Level 3 attestations, and patches CVEs under an SLA (seven days for critical issues, usually 48-72 hours). It plugs into JFrog, Nexus or GitHub Packages. Java, JavaScript and Python are covered now, with Go, Rust and PHP planned for early next year. End-of-life packages move to Endless Lifecycle Support, which also covers operating systems and runtimes. KernelCare and LibraryCare patch in memory without reboots. TuxCare also supports AlmaLinux, and was spun off from CloudLinux on 1 January.
keyPoints: Sellen claimed TuxCare sometimes shipped fixes for recent Linux CVEs two to three days before the original vendors.
SecureChain covers all direct and transitive dependencies of an ecosystem under one subscription, and works with your existing repository manager without new agents, CI changes or dashboards.
Endless Lifecycle Support runs for as long as the customer needs it; Sellen cited a customer still on CentOS 6, and said TuxCare will add any free open-source component on request.
KernelCare live patching lets teams patch during business hours. Sellen cited a customer whose CentOS server ran eight years without a reboot, until the hardware was retired.
takeaways: Check how many of your production dependencies and base images are past upstream end of life, and decide whether to upgrade or buy extended support.
If you evaluate a curated package repository, ask for SBOM, VEX and SLSA evidence and compare its CVE SLAs against your own patch times.
watchIf: You are responsible for end-of-life Linux or open-source dependencies and want an overview of TuxCare's commercial offering; there is no technical depth or demo.
